title: Handi Chicken
description: A rich North Indian chicken curry with deeply browned onions, tomatoes, yogurt, coriander, green chilies, kasuri methi, and a creamy finish.
steps: Heat the ghee in a heavy-bottomed handi or deep pan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and cook slowly until they become deep golden brown.
Remove the browned onions from the pan and set them aside.
In the same ghee, add the chopped garlic and cook for about 30 seconds without letting it burn.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until completely soft and beginning to release their oil.
Return the browned onions to the pan and mix well.
Add the ginger paste and cook for another minute.
Add the cumin seeds, lightly crushed coriander seeds, and green chilies.
Add the turmeric powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, and salt. Mix well.
Add the chicken thighs and cook over medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until the chicken is lightly browned.
Cover and cook for about 5 minutes so the chicken releases some of its juices.
Reduce the heat to low. Gradually add the whisked yogurt while stirring continuously so it does not split.
Cook for 8-10 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and the gravy becomes thick and glossy.
Crush the Kasoori methi between your palms and stir it into the curry.
For a richer version, stir in the heavy cream and cook gently for another 2-3 minutes.
Rest the handi chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Cook the onions until genuinely deep golden brown; they provide much of the body and sweetness of the gravy.
Chicken thighs work particularly well because they remain juicy during the longer cooking process.
Keep the heat low when adding yogurt to reduce the chance of it splitting.
Lightly crushing the coriander seeds instead of using coriander powder gives the curry a more distinctive handi-style texture and aroma.
Add the Kasoori methi and garam masala near the end so their aromas remain prominent.
Heavy cream is optional. Without it, the yogurt and browned onions still produce a rich gravy.
Serve with naan, tandoori roti, paratha, or jeera rice.
